Add Interval-Level Covariates to a Distance-Removal Frame

Source: R/prepare_gdr_intervals.R
prepare_gdr_intervals.Rd

Add covariates that can change from one removal interval to the next, such as who was listening in each interval, to a copy of an unmarkedFrameGDR. Rows are matched by survey identifier and interval number, so the input can be in any order, and the alignment is recorded.

Usage

prepare_gdr_intervals(
  object,
  event_keys,
  event_id,
  interval_data,
  interval_units,
  interval = "interval",
  site_id = NULL,
  effort = NULL,
  expected_event_keys = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'msr_gdr_intervals'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

object

An unmarkedFrameGDR with its original counts and its site, yearly and observation covariates.

event_keys

A data frame with one row per survey event, in the frame's order (all primary periods of the first frame row, then the second, and so on). Use the original survey identifiers. The names .input_row, .input_row_name and .interval are reserved.

event_id

Character vector naming the column(s) of event_keys that identify each survey.

interval_data

A data frame with the event_id columns, the interval number column and the new covariates. It needs exactly one row for every survey and removal interval. Rows can be in any order, and alignment records how they were matched.

interval_units

Character string naming the time unit of the removal intervals, such as "minutes". No time conversion is performed.

interval

Character string, default "interval". The name of the interval number column in interval_data. Its values must be whole numbers from 1 to the number of removal intervals per primary period. The column is also added to the observation covariates, so formulas can use it.

site_id

Optional column(s) of event_keys that identify the physical site, passed to validate_unmarked_data(). Frame rows need not be physical sites.

effort

Optional numeric vector of survey effort, one value per event, passed to validate_unmarked_data(). Positive values mark completed surveys, zero marks unsurveyed events and NA marks unknown effort.

expected_event_keys

Optional independent event list in frame order, passed to validate_unmarked_data().

x

A prepared msr_gdr_intervals object to print.

...

Not used.

Value

A list of class msr_gdr_intervals:

  • data: a copy of object with the new observation covariates.

  • survey_audit: the result of validate_unmarked_data() for the frame.

  • alignment: one row per observation row in frame order, with the event (.event), frame row (.site_row), primary period (.primary), interval (.interval), the matching row of interval_data (.input_row, .input_row_name) and the event_keys columns.

  • protocol: the survey protocol from the audit (units, distance breaks, interval lengths), plus the frame dimensions, the interval_column, the added_columns, any added names that also occur among the site or yearly covariates (shared_site_or_annual_names), whether the input order changed (reordered) and the unmarked version.

  • fit_eligibility_established: always FALSE.

Printing reports the dimensions and whether the input order changed, and returns the object invisibly. If the survey audit finds an error, or the interval rows cannot be aligned, the function stops with a condition of class msr_gdr_interval_error carrying survey_audit and the offending input_rows. The input frame is never changed.

How rows are aligned

unmarked orders observation rows by frame row, primary period and then removal interval, and its own setter for observation covariates does not check that order. This function checks the keys first. It rejects unknown, duplicate, missing or extra survey and interval combinations, and any attempt to overwrite an existing observation column. The event identifier columns are used only for matching. Every other column of interval_data, including the interval number, is added.

The counts, existing covariates, distance bands, interval lengths, units, column classes, factor levels and contrasts are unchanged. Missing values are kept, and unmarked applies its own missing-data rules when fitting. Nothing is aggregated or imputed. Added names that also occur among the site or yearly covariates are recorded for review. Use distinct names for fields with different meanings, because multiScale_optim() will not estimate a scale for a site covariate whose name is shadowed this way.

Model the first interval

Use formulas such as ~ I(interval == 1) or ~ factor(interval) when the observation process justifies them. With equal unit intervals, hazards pi in the first interval and b thereafter reproduce the first-time law of a simple encounter Markov process regardless of persistence after an encounter. First times alone do not estimate that persistence or establish a finite corrected density. Unequal durations keep their per-unit probability interpretation. Keep linked complete histories when assessing re-detections. This function only arranges data. It adds no model terms, parameters or uncertainty methods.

For covariates that are constant within a survey, expand_gdr_intervals() builds interval_data for you.

See also

expand_gdr_intervals(), validate_unmarked_data(), prepare_gdr_histories()

Examples

frame <- unmarked::unmarkedFrameGDR(
  yDistance = matrix(c(1, 0, 0, 1), 2, byrow = TRUE),
  yRemoval = matrix(c(1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0), 2, byrow = TRUE),
  siteCovs = data.frame(site = factor(c("A", "B"))),
  dist.breaks = c(0, 25, 75), unitsIn = "m",
  period.lengths = c(1, 2, 1))
keys <- data.frame(site = c("A", "B"), survey = c("s1", "s2"))
# One row per survey and interval, deliberately out of frame order
bands <- data.frame(survey = rep(c("s2", "s1"), each = 3),
  interval = rep(c(3, 1, 2), 2),
  observer = factor(c("Ann", "Ann", "Bob", "Bob", "Ann", "Ann")))
prepared <- prepare_gdr_intervals(frame, keys, "survey", bands,
  interval_units = "minutes", site_id = "site")
# Observer and interval number, now in frame order
unmarked::obsCovs(prepared$data)
#>   interval observer
#> 1        1      Ann
#> 2        2      Ann
#> 3        3      Bob
#> 4        1      Ann
#> 5        2      Bob
#> 6        3      Ann
# Which input row filled each observation row
prepared$alignment[, c(".event", ".interval", ".input_row", "survey")]
#>   .event .interval .input_row survey
#> 1      1         1          5     s1
#> 2      1         2          6     s1
#> 3      1         3          4     s1
#> 4      2         1          2     s2
#> 5      2         2          3     s2
#> 6      2         3          1     s2
